question: On 21 January 2025, the Commission, in partnership with the Polish Presidency of the Council of the EU, organised the Holocaust Remembrance Conference, ‘Remembering the Past. Shaping the future’. European Jews for Palestine (EJP), a European Jewish umbrella organisation with 20 affiliated groups in 13 EU Member States, did not receive an invitation. The organisation’s requests to participate were formally refused.

On 20 January 2025 the Commission’s coordinator apparently replied to the EJP to say that ‘the invitations are based on the organisations’ expertise on Holocaust education and remembrance’, and that the focus of EJP ‘does not align closely to the specific context’.
However, among those reportedly invited to the event were representatives of the lobby group European Leadership Network (ELNET), and also of Google and the Anglican Church. 1.
On the basis of what criteria did the Commission conclude that EJP does not have sufficient focus on Holocaust remembrance and education?
Can the Commission explain how Google and ELNET better meet the aforementioned criteria?
What ‘specific context’ does the Commission consider the European Jewish umbrella organisation EJP does not align with closely enough?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.9.2025) The Commission marked the 80th anniversary of the liberation Nazi death camp AuschwitzBirkenau by hosting the Holocaust Remembrance Conference: Remembering the past. Shaping the future, in partnership with the Polish Presidency of the Council of the EU, on 21 January 2025.

This is a key deliverable under the EU Strategy on Combating Antisemitism and fostering Jewish life. The Holocaust Remembrance Conference aimed at honouring the victims of the Shoah and their memory. On 21 January 2025, the Commission organised the conference in partnership with the Polish Presidency of the Council of the EU.

The testimony of a survivor of Ravensbrück and Bergen-Belsen was centre stage, together with young Europeans reading poems and letters of victims. The Commission seeks to ensure a balanced representation in the events it is organising. The organisations invited are engaged in the fight against antisemitism and in countering Holocaust distortion.

In this case, it declined the request of European Jews for Palestine (EJP) to be a partner organisation given that the information provided by the organisation in their letters and Transparency Register1 did not show how their mission and expertise would support the objectives of the conference. The EJP was invited to participate in the Holocaust Remembrance conference online, as it was livestreamed.
Contrary to the Honourable Member’s query, Google was not invited to the event.
